A **BOOX Picco-only** test release. It is `v2.0.0-library-sync.2` (CrossInk v2.0.0 with OPDS library sync and EB Garamond) plus the Picco display work from CrossPoint's second Picco beta, and one addition of this fork's: anti-aliased text on pages that have a picture.

Only `firmware-picco.bin` is attached. Every other reader should stay on [`v2.0.0-library-sync.2`](https://github.com/HannahTheSpanner/crossink-library-sync/releases/tag/v2.0.0-library-sync.2).

> **Not yet run on a Picco.** GitHub Actions built this image and the host tests pass, but nothing here has been tested on hardware. Keep the `firmware-picco.bin` from `v2.0.0-library-sync.2` to hand so you can go back.

## Install

`firmware-picco.bin` is an application image for the Picco's `app` slot (offset `0xE0000`), not a full flash image. Install it only with a USB installer that explicitly supports the BOOX Picco, and never erase the device or write a factory image: the Picco's recovery software must stay intact. See [docs/picco.md](https://github.com/HannahTheSpanner/crossink-library-sync/blob/feat/picco-beta2-display/docs/picco.md).

## Added

- **Anti-aliased text on picture pages.** A page with a picture is drawn with the panel's four-shade image waveform. The page's text was plain black and white there, so it looked heavier than on other pages, most often on the first page of a chapter. The text's soft edges now use the two greys of that same waveform. Nothing changes with Text Anti-Aliasing off or with Images set to Display (B&W).
- **Battery strip on the sleep screen.** Asleep on USB power, a battery strip is drawn over a sleep screen that shows a four-shade picture, such as a cover, and removed when the reader is unplugged. It needs a panel driver that can repaint part of such a picture (the SSD1677 panels); other sleep screens are left untouched, as before.

## Changed

- **Display driver.** The FreeInk SDK moves to the revision CrossInk pins for this work (`aad0749`). Its Picco display driver is the one in CrossPoint's second Picco beta, which CrossPoint describes as better picture rendering, less ghosting, a better night mode and faster refreshes.
- **Reading waveform.** Book pages tell the display when they are being shown, so the panel uses its reading waveform for page turns, and the first menu drawn over a page erases it cleanly.
- **Pictures** in EPUBs are drawn with the panel's four-shade image waveform.
- **Sunlight Fading Fix** is no longer offered or applied on the Picco. It compensates the Xteink X3 and X4 waveforms only.

## What to check on the device

1. Open a book whose chapters start with a picture, with Text Anti-Aliasing on. The text under the picture should have the same weight as the text on the next page, and should not change half a second after the page appears.
2. Compare the edge greys on that page with a text-only page. They come from the image waveform, not the text one, so a slightly lighter or darker edge is possible.
3. Turn several text-only pages, open and close the reader menu over a page, and try night mode: look for ghosting or leftover text.
4. Put a bookmark on a picture page and check the confirmation message and the status bar draw cleanly.
5. Sleep on a cover sleep screen with USB plugged in, then unplug.

If anything looks wrong, flash `firmware-picco.bin` from `v2.0.0-library-sync.2` again.

## Not included

- Firmware for the other readers. The same SDK revision changes their display drivers too (one-pass text anti-aliasing on the X4 Pro and X4 Classic among them); the branch builds for all of them, but none of that is released or tested here.
- CrossPoint's change that clears the screen to white before drawing a sleep screen.
- Features added to CrossPoint's `develop` branch after 2.0.0 that are not display work.

## Where it comes from

- The Picco display work is CrossPoint Reader's (pull request 4362 there, by Justin Mitchell) and the FreeInk SDK's.
- This release takes it as CrossInk ported it: the display parts of commit `48d44219` in uxjulia/crossink, by Julia Nguyen.
- The text anti-aliasing on picture pages, and any mistakes in fitting these together, belong to this fork.
